title: History Quiz
midCtaText: Enjoying the quiz? Subscribe & hit the bell!
subscribeText: New quiz every day – turn on the bell 🔔

questions.q: Which ancient people built the **Parthenon**?
questions.fact: Built in Athens about 2,450 years ago to honour Athena.

questions.q: Who sailed to the Americas in **1492**?
questions.fact: He crossed with three ships: Niña, Pinta and Santa María.

questions.q: Ancient **Egyptians** preserved their dead as…?
questions.fact: Making a mummy could take around 70 days.

questions.q: The **Great Wall** was built in which country?
questions.fact: A 2012 survey measured all its parts at about 21,196 km.

questions.q: **Gladiators** fought in the arenas of…?
questions.fact: Most gladiators were slaves or prisoners of war.

questions.q: **Samurai** were warriors from which country?
questions.fact: Samurai were officially abolished in the 1870s.

questions.q: Where did the ancient **Olympic Games** begin?
questions.fact: The first recorded Games at Olympia date to 776 BC.

questions.q: Which city was buried by **Vesuvius** in 79 AD?
questions.fact: The ash preserved bread, graffiti and whole streets.

questions.q: Who was killed on the **Ides of March**?
questions.fact: The Ides of March is 15 March. Caesar died in 44 BC.

questions.q: The **Vikings** came mainly from…?
questions.fact: Vikings reached North America about 500 years before Columbus.

questions.q: Which people built **Chichen Itza**?
questions.fact: Its main pyramid has 365 steps – one for each day.

questions.q: Who ruled England when the **Armada** attacked?
questions.fact: The Spanish Armada sailed against England in 1588.

questions.q: Which English king had **six wives**?
questions.fact: Only two of his six wives were executed.

questions.q: What linked China to Europe for **trade**?
questions.fact: It was a network of routes, not a single road.

questions.q: In which year did the **French Revolution** begin?
questions.fact: It began with the storming of the Bastille on 14 July.

questions.q: Who printed with **movable metal type** in Europe?
questions.fact: His famous Bible was printed around the 1450s.

questions.q: Which Viking reached **North America** first?
questions.fact: A Viking site was found at L'Anse aux Meadows in Canada.

questions.q: In which century did the **Black Death** hit Europe?
questions.fact: It killed perhaps a third or more of Europe's people.

questions.q: **Joan of Arc** fought for which country?
questions.fact: She was only about 19 when she died in 1431.

questions.q: Who founded the **Mongol** Empire?
questions.fact: It became the largest connected land empire in history.

questions.q: What was the capital of the **Byzantine** Empire?
questions.fact: Today the city is called Istanbul.

questions.q: Which emperor was buried with a **clay army**?
questions.fact: The Terracotta Army has thousands of life-size soldiers.

questions.q: **Suleiman the Magnificent** ruled which empire?
questions.fact: He ruled for 46 years, from 1520 to 1566.

questions.q: What did the Romans call **London**?
questions.fact: Romans founded it around AD 47.

questions.q: The **Hanging Gardens** were said to be in…?
questions.fact: No one has ever found clear proof they existed.

questions.q: Whose expedition first sailed **around the world**?
questions.fact: Magellan died on the way; Elcano finished in 1522.

questions.q: The ruins of **Troy** are in which country?
questions.fact: Troy lies at Hisarlik, in northwest Turkey.

questions.q: Which people built **Tenochtitlan**?
questions.fact: Mexico City stands on its ruins today.

questions.q: Who crossed the **Alps** with elephants?
questions.fact: The Carthaginian general did it in 218 BC.

questions.q: Who first reached the **South Pole**?
questions.fact: Amundsen's team arrived on 14 December 1911.

questions.q: **York** and **Lancaster** fought in which war?
questions.fact: York had a white rose, Lancaster a red one.

questions.q: First lasting English **town** in America (1607)?
questions.fact: Jamestown, Virginia, was founded in 1607.

questions.q: The **Colossus** stood on which Greek island?
questions.fact: An earthquake toppled it after only about 54 years.

questions.q: In which year did the **Western Roman Empire** fall?
questions.fact: In 476 the last emperor, Romulus Augustulus, was removed.

questions.q: What was the capital of the **Inca** Empire?
questions.fact: Cusco sits about 3,400 m above sea level.

questions.q: Who wrote about the court of **Kublai Khan**?
questions.fact: He said he spent about 17 years in China.

questions.q: Which ancient wonder was a giant **lighthouse**?
questions.fact: The Pharos was among the tallest buildings of its time.

questions.q: Who founded the **Mughal** Empire in India?
questions.fact: Babur won the First Battle of Panipat in 1526.

questions.q: Which dynasty built most of today's **Great Wall**?
questions.fact: Most sections tourists visit today are Ming-era.

questions.q: Which city-state fought at **Thermopylae** in 480 BC?
questions.fact: King Leonidas led the famous 300 Spartans.

questions.q: Which emperor built the **Hagia Sophia** in 537?
questions.fact: For about 1,000 years it was the largest cathedral.

questions.q: Which people carved **Petra** in Jordan?
questions.fact: Petra is carved straight into rose-red sandstone cliffs.

questions.q: Which peace ended the **Thirty Years' War**?
questions.fact: The Peace of Westphalia was signed in 1648.

questions.q: **Mansa Musa** ruled which empire?
questions.fact: His 1324 pilgrimage to Mecca was famous for its gold.

questions.q: Which English king was executed in **1649**?
questions.fact: England then had no king for 11 years.

questions.q: Which Roman emperor built a wall across **Britain**?
questions.fact: Work on Hadrian's Wall began around AD 122.

questions.q: Which empire built **Angkor Wat**?
questions.fact: It's the largest religious monument in the world.

questions.q: Who invented **cuneiform** writing?
questions.fact: Cuneiform was pressed into clay over 5,000 years ago.

questions.q: **Alexander the Great** was king of…?
questions.fact: He was tutored as a boy by Aristotle.

questions.q: In which year did **Constantinople** fall?
questions.fact: Ottoman forces took the city on 29 May 1453.
